✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The area contains Peninsular Malaysia, Southern Thailand, and the southernmost tip of Myanmar (Kawthaung).

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: The island country of _____ also has historical and cultural ties with the region
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The island country of Singapore also has historical and cultural ties with the region. The Strait of Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula from the Indonesian island of Sumatra, and the south coast is separated from the island of Singapore by the Straits of Johor.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: It is frequently mentioned in the _____, a well-known classic tale associated with the legendary heroes of Malacca Sultanate
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: It is frequently mentioned in the Hikayat Hang Tuah, a well-known classic tale associated with the legendary heroes of Malacca Sultanate.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: Tanah Melayu in the text is consistently employed to refer to the area under _____ dominance
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: Tanah Melayu in the text is consistently employed to refer to the area under Malaccan dominance.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: In the Negarakertagama manuscript written in _____, this area is called Hujung Medini
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: In the Negarakertagama manuscript written in 1365, this area is called Hujung Medini.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: The Sumatran rhinoceros (Dicerorhinus sumatrensis) once inhabited the forests, but Malaysia's last rhinoceroses died in _____, and the species' few remaining members survive only in Sumatra
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The Sumatran rhinoceros (Dicerorhinus sumatrensis) once inhabited the forests, but Malaysia's last rhinoceroses died in 2019, and the species' few remaining members survive only in Sumatra.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: The forests north of the boundary are characterized by seasonally-deciduous trees, while the _____ forests have more year-round rainfall and the trees are mostly evergreen
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The Kangar-Pattani floristic boundary crosses the peninsula in southern Thailand and northernmost Malaysia, marking the boundary between the large biogeographic regions of Indochina to the north and Sundaland and Malesia to the south. The forests north of the boundary are characterized by seasonally-deciduous trees, while the Sundaland forests have more year-round rainfall and the trees are mostly evergreen.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: The lowlands and hills are in the _____ rain forests ecoregion
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The Peninsular Malaysian montane rain forests ecoregion covers the mountains above 1,000 meters elevation. The lowlands and hills are in the Peninsular Malaysian rain forests ecoregion.

✓ Malay Peninsula.subject: World Geography
✓ Malay Peninsula.question: The Myanmar Coast mangroves are on the western shore of the peninsula, and the _____ mangroves on the eastern shore
✓ Malay Peninsula.fact: The Myanmar Coast mangroves are on the western shore of the peninsula, and the Indochina mangroves on the eastern shore.
